Virtual try-on algorithm integrating multi-view user perspectives with multi-level sampling warping module (M-LSWM)
abstract: Virtual try-on technology holds considerable potential for application within the e-commerce and fashion sectors. By utilizing digital superimposition techniques to achieve precise virtual garment fitting, this technology not only enhances the consumer shopping experience but also transforms the nature of consumer interaction. Nevertheless, current approaches frequently encounter challenges such as loss of detail, texture distortion, and limited adaptability to diverse postures, leading to discrepancies between the synthesized images and the actual fitting experience. To address these limitations, this study introduces a novel virtual try-on algorithm that integrates multi-view user data with a Multi-Level Sampling Warping Module (M-LSWM). Initially, a multi-view input model is designed to capture essential user informationincluding body shape, proportions, and contoursfrom multiple perspectives. Subsequently, the M-LSWM is employed to warp clothing images, facilitating precise alignment between garments and user images while maintaining critical details such as fine textures and edges. Finally, a BoTNet-based generator network is utilized to extract local features, including edges and textures, thereby generating high-quality virtual try-on images. Experimental evaluations conducted on the DressCode and VITON-HD datasets demonstrate that the proposed algorithm surpasses existing methods in both image quality and realism.

title: Distributed multi-sensor data fusion for multi-target tracking in rescue missions
Fatigue-consistent wind turbine load reconstruction via physics-guided differentiable spectral fatigue modelling
abstract: Accurate fatigue life estimation is essential for reliable operation and maintenance of wind turbines, but direct measurement of fatigue-critical loads is often challenging due to cost and durability constraints on strain-gauge instrumentation. Existing machine-learning-based load reconstruction methods are generally trained to optimise pointwise signal accuracy; however, fatigue damage accumulation is predominantly governed by cyclic and spectral characteristics rather than by instantaneous reconstruction fidelity alone. Moreover, standard fatigue measures derived from rainflow counting are fundamentally non-differentiable, which prevents their direct integration within gradient-based learning schemes. To overcome this drawback, this work develops an LSTM-based virtual sensing framework to reconstruct full time-resolved tower base fore-aft bending moment histories using SCADA-based parameters and nacelle acceleration signals. The core novelty lies in a composite optimisation objective that combines mean squared error with a differentiable spectral fatigue loss based on Dirlik’s method, thereby jointly enforcing local time-domain accuracy and global fatigue-relevant spectral consistency. Trained and validated on OpenFAST aeroelastic simulations of the IEA 15-MW reference turbine, the proposed model explains more than 99% of the variance in mean tower base loads and accurately reproduces downstream fatigue metrics. The propagation of signal reconstruction errors is quantified across the pipeline to establish explicit error bounds for damage-equivalent loads (DEL) and equivalent fatigue loads (EFL). A systematic noise robustness study, based on injecting controlled levels of Gaussian noise into individual input features, further reveals that the model is more sensitive to noise in blade pitch and generator speed, which directly define the aerodynamic operating state, but remains markedly more tolerant to measurement degradation in nacelle acceleration and wind speed inputs. These results link virtual sensor performance to realistic sensor signal-to-noise ratios and offer practical guidance on sensor quality and filtering requirements. Overall, the proposed framework provides a concise, physics-guided route to integrate fatigue specific constraints into virtual sensing frameworks, enabling condition-based maintenance and life extension strategies.

Active learning for interactive prompt clarification in safety-critical programmable logic controller code generation
abstract: Large language models (LLM) enable automated program synthesis, but their application in safety-critical Industrial Control Systems (ICS) is constrained by specification imprecision and non-deterministic logic drift. This study addresses these challenges by integrating Active Learning (AL) as a decision-governance layer for Interactive Prompt Clarification (IPC) in Programmable Logic Controller (PLC) code generation. We treat requirements-to-code synthesis as a soft-computing problem of reasoning under uncertainty, where missing specifications are quantified as first-class uncertainty signals.The proposed methodology, IPC+AL, implements a policy-level controller that measures logical ambiguity through entropy derived from multi-validator disagreement. This approach transforms code synthesis into a budgeted value-of-information (VOI) policy that determines when to query for clarification and when to terminate the synthesis loop deterministically. By embedding uncertainty quantification and fail-closed gating into the generative process, the framework ensures code emission occurs only when safety and dialect constraints are met.Evaluation across industrial PLC case studies—including batch mixing and robotic pick-and-place tasks—demonstrates that uncertainty-guided clarification produces an "entropy-collapse" effect, consistently shifting solutions toward verified safety thresholds. Comparisons with standard prompting and passive clarification show higher gate pass-rates and superior cost-performance trade-offs. Validation via Inter-Rater Reliability (IRR) metrics (Cohen’s kappa and Krippendorff’s alpha) confirms that IPC+AL provides an auditable, evaluator-invariant policy for certification-oriented synthesis in safety-critical industrial settings.

Beyond prediction: Interval neural networks for uncertainty-aware system identification
abstract: System identification (SysID) is critical for modeling dynamical systems from experimental data, yet traditional approaches often fail to capture nonlinear behaviors. While deep learning offers powerful tools for modeling such dynamics, incorporating uncertainty quantification is essential to ensure reliable predictions. This paper presents a systematic framework for constructing and training interval Neural Networks (INNs) for uncertainty-aware SysID. By extending crisp neural networks into interval counterparts, we develop Interval LSTM and NODE models that propagate uncertainty through interval arithmetic without probabilistic assumptions. This design allows them to represent uncertainty and produce prediction intervals. For training, we propose two strategies: Cascade INN (C-INN), a two-stage approach converting a trained crisp NN into an INN, and Joint INN (J-INN), a one-stage framework jointly optimizing prediction accuracy and interval precision. Both strategies employ uncertainty-aware loss functions and parameterization tricks to ensure reliable learning. Comprehensive experiments on multiple SysID datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of both approaches and benchmark their performance against well-established uncertainty-aware baselines: C-INN achieves superior point prediction accuracy, whereas J-INN yields more accurate and better-calibrated prediction intervals. Furthermore, to reveal how uncertainty is represented across model parameters, the concept of channel-wise elasticity is introduced, which is used to identify distinct patterns across the two training strategies. The results of this study demonstrate that the proposed framework effectively integrates deep learning with uncertainty-aware modeling.

abstract: This paper presents a novel pipeline for 3D coronary artery reconstruction from two-view X-ray projections. The methodology consists of an initial backprojection to retrieve a 3D point cloud approximation, followed by a refinement stage using a classifier-free guidance (CFG) diffusion model. The model was trained on synthetic data from the ImageCAS dataset and evaluated on both synthetic and 100 clinical samples. A key contribution of this work is an extensive ablation study on model variants and a detailed examination environment sensitivity analysis. Contrary to initial design assumptions, results demonstrate that for the right coronary artery, a side-agnostic model (trained on both left and right arteries) outperforms side-specific alternatives, while for the left artery, omitting projection conditioning yields the best results. In the proposed synthetic data-based evaluation framework, the best variant achieved a D S C 3 D of 0.33 for the right side, 0.28 for the left side; O 3 D ( 1 ) = 0.59 for the right side, 0.51 for the left side; O 3 D ( 2 ) = 0.78 and 0.70 for the left side. A significant improvement in qualitative factors of the reconstruction on clinical data was observed. This work provides a generative alternative to traditional reconstruction methods, addressing their primary limitations, using a strong geometric prior as scaffolding and reaching current state-of-the-art.

title: Hybrid entropy–fuzzy weighted decision matrix (HEF-WDM) for the optimal software architecture pattern selection
abstract: In software development the software architecture pattern has a direct impact on the number of system characteristics including scalability, adaptability, and maintainability. Consequently, selecting an appropriate software architecture is a crucial decision. Such decision is complex because of conflicting criteria and uncertainty in expert judgment. This study seeks to propose a systematic and objective decision matrix for the selection of optimal software architecture patterns by addressing performance evaluation uncertainty and bias in criterion weighting. A hybrid Entropy based Fuzzy VIKOR multi criteria decision making model is developed. An originality, the paper develops a Hybrid Entropy-Fuzzy Weighted Decision Matrix (HEF-WDM) where entropy-based objective weights are integrated into fuzzy decision process. This mechanism avoid early defuzzification, enforces data-driven objectivity, and maintains expert uncertainty. An academic portal case study that evaluates a six software architecture patterns against eight criteria is used to validate the proposed decision matrix. According to the results, Event Driven Architecture (Q=0.000) score lowest compromise index, followed by the Microservices Architecture (0.073). Sensitive analysis verifies that the ranking is resilient to changes in weight. The finding show that the proposed decision matrix improves decision reliability, reduces subjective bias, and offers a rigorous, unbiased, and flexible method for selecting software architecture. The results show that integrating entropy weighting within the fuzzy domain produces reliable and rational architectural decisions. Beyond academic portals, the proposed decision matrix can be generalized to support the selection of suitable software architectures across different fields of system design.

PPIE-Net: Physics-inspired parametric input embedding for data-efficient surrogate modeling of parametric simulations
abstract: Differential equations (DEs) are essential for modeling and simulating complex physical processes in engineering. While traditional numerical methods provide high-fidelity solutions, their prohibitive computational cost for repeated parametric studies hinders real-time engineering evaluation. Recently, deep learning-based models have emerged as efficient alternatives; however, their architectural complexity and heavy reliance on massive datasets often limit their practical tractability, leading to high solution costs in data-constrained engineering applications. To address these challenges, this research proposes a novel neuro-computing surrogate framework incorporating a P hysics-inspired P arametric I nput E mbedding (PPIE) scheme. By explicitly encoding the multiplicative interactions between spatiotemporal coordinates and physical parameters, PPIE introduces a powerful architectural inductive bias that mirrors fundamental physical scaling laws, achieving enhanced robustness with minimal network scale. We demonstrate that the proposed PPIE-Net with a minimalist Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) architecture matches or outperforms state-of-the-art neural operators and physics-informed models, such as DeepONet, Fourier Neural Operators (FNO), Convolutional Neural Operators (CNO), and Parametric Physics-Informed Neural Networks (P-PINNs), particularly in extreme data-scarce scenarios ( N ≤ 20 ). Our results across five representative DE domains—including a complex 3D laser processing application—show that the proposed framework enables accurate predictions even in such data-constrained environments with significantly reduced computational overhead; this facilitates real-time system modeling, engineering analysis, and optimization. This work offers a highly efficient, robust, and scalable soft computing pathway for real-world multi-physics engineering problems.

Physics-based and machine learning–integrated analysis of adjustable multi-pad journal bearings under load-between-pad configuration
abstract: Multi-pad adjustable/active journal bearings offer significant flexibility in controlling hydrodynamic performance through radial and tilt pad adjustments. However, their strongly nonlinear and coupled behaviour poses challenges for efficient performance prediction. In this study, a comprehensive physics-based and machine learning–integrated framework is developed to analyze and predict the steady-state characteristics of 3-pad and 4-pad adjustable journal bearings operating under load-between-pad (LBP) configuration. The hydrodynamic pressure field is obtained by solving the non-dimensional Reynolds equation using a finite difference method coupled with an iterative pressure–attitude angle convergence scheme. Static performance characteristics, including maximum pressure, load capacity, attitude angle, frictional force, friction variable, and flow rate, are evaluated over a wide range of eccentricity ratios, radial adjustments, tilt angles, and number of pads. The resulting comprehensive dataset is subsequently employed to train multi-output surrogate models using Artificial Neural Networks (ANN), Gaussian Process Regression (GPR), and Support Vector Regression (SVR). Bayesian hyperparameter optimization with cross-validation is adopted to ensure robust model generalization. The comparative analysis indicates that GPR provides the highest predictive accuracy, the lowest error dispersion, and the most consistent performance within the investigated operating domain. Parametric response surface analysis using GPR model shows that eccentricity ratio is the dominant factor governing load capacity, pressure, frictional behavior, and lubricant flow. Radial adjustment effectively controls clearance and leakage, with negative adjustment improving load support and frictional efficiency, while positive adjustment enhances flow and cooling at the expense of load capacity. Tilt adjustment was found to influence pressure asymmetry and attitude angle at low to moderate eccentricities, with reduced impact at higher loads. The proposed framework provides a computationally efficient approach for rapid prediction and design-space exploration of adjustable journal bearing performance.

title: Ghost Rate: A pre-training geometric quality diagnostic for synthetic oversampling in imbalanced text classification
Transformer-based integrated prediction model for copper converter blowing endpoint and composition
Graph-based collaborative multi-agent deep reinforcement learning for reconfigurable job shop scheduling
abstract: Dynamically reconfiguring machines to accommodate a wider range of tasks is critical for manufacturers adapting to personalized customization. Thus, this paper addresses the job shop scheduling problem with machine function reconfiguration, while accounting for constraints on limited auxiliary modules and limited extended processing functions. A mixed-integer linear programming model considering the supportability of processing functions and the availability of limited and shareable auxiliary modules is formulated. To solve this problem efficiently, a graph-based collaborative multi-agent deep reinforcement learning model (CG-DRL) is developed, in which two complementary heterogeneous graph models are designed for job scheduling and machine function reconfiguration, respectively, and a collaborative duel agent learning framework considering prior decision knowledge learned from the opposite agent is proposed to guide state design and reduce state/action space. A rule-based initial replay buffer is created to reduce meaningless exploration by building structured experience data from the state-specific decision pattern knowledge hidden in gene expression programming-discovered problem-specific rules. Besides, a reward-based decision space reducer is designed to identify key decision genes and inherit good prior decision genes to cut computation and retrain poor ones for better performance. Experiments prove that both the proposed replay buffer creation and decision space reduction mechanisms are effective. By integrating these mechanisms, the proposed CG-DRL significantly outperforms other baselines, including empirical dispatching rules, Double deep Q network, and CG-DRL variants.

title: Service-effort trade-offs in large-scale bike-sharing rebalancing: A hierarchical reinforcement learning framework with imitation-based warm-starting
abstract: Large-scale Bike-Sharing Systems (BSS) exhibit spatiotemporal demand imbalances that challenge real-time control. Although Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) offers adaptivity, flat city-wide controllers face combinatorial action spaces and unstable training. We propose a bi-level framework separating local spatial encoding and potential intra-region stabilization from global inter-region coordination. Regional agents encode inventory, pressure, and weather through multi-channel heatmaps and Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), while a masked actor-critic policy allocates bicycles between regions. The global controller is initialized by Behavior Cloning (BC) from a heuristic teacher and refined by reinforcement learning (RL) using a cost-aware service–effort reward. The Warsaw Veturilo system (365 stations, May–November 2023) is a high-baseline setting: passive operation already achieves 89.21 ± 0.51% service rate. A five-seed ablation shows that tabula rasa RL is unstable, whereas BC-initialized variants remain stable in service rate and substantially reduce the incidence of extreme relocation regimes. BC-only achieved the highest mean city-wide service rate (89.47 ± 0.50%), while BC+RL achieved a comparable rate (89.36 ± 0.41%) with approximately 41% lower relocation volume than BC-only. A dedicated representation ablation further shows that the CNN-based hybrid encoder yields no statistically significant service-rate advantage over a vector-only baseline; its value lies in providing a fixed-size, spatially structured, and scalable state encoding rather than in measurable performance gains. Overall, the framework combines scalability, training stability, and lower relocation effort at comparable service quality.

Integrating time-series data image representation with efficient multi-scale feature extraction for human activity recognition
abstract: Human activity recognition (HAR) based on wearable sensors has been widely applied in intelligent healthcare, sports health due to its advantages in low power consumption, real-time performance, and privacy preservation. Recently, advanced approaches have focused on transforming time-series data into images and leveraging deep learning for recognition, which solves the problem of one-sidedness of information and dependence on data quality in traditional one-dimensional processing. However, existing image representation methods of time-series data only capture single-dimensional features resulting in the loss of key information and complex operations. Moreover, the adopted deep learning architectures are still largely confined to conventional models, resulting in insufficient ability to capture multi-scale features. To address the above problem, this study proposes a human activity recognition framework that integrates time-series data image representation (TIR) with an efficient multi-scale feature extraction network (EMFENet). The framework first utilizes wavelet transform to efficiently encode time-series data into images. We then introduce a multi-branch wavelet transform convolution (MWTC) to achieve lightweight multi-scale feature extraction. We further employ a cross-space multi-scale attention mechanism (CSMA) to enhance critical information and design a multi-scale dilated convolution (MSDC) to capture long-range dependencies within the image, complete spatial context modeling, and provide more robust semantic information for subsequent classification. The effectiveness of the model is validated on 6 public HAR datasets (UCI-HAR, WISDM, PAMAP2, OPPORTUNITY, UniMiB-SHAR, USC-HAD). The experimental results demonstrate that TIR-EMFENet achieves competitive recognition performance while maintaining low model complexity.

TransfoRhythm: A transformer architecture conductive to blood pressure estimation through solo PPG signal capturing
abstract: Recent statistics indicate that approximately billion individuals worldwide are affected by hypertension, a major contributor to premature mortality. Blood pressure (BP) is an important physiological indicator for hypertension assessment and management. Conventional cuff-based methods provide intermittent measurements and may be unsuitable for continuous monitoring. Recent advances in artificial intelligence (AI) and deep neural networks (DNNs) have therefore increased interest in data-driven cuff-less BP estimation. Existing studies frequently combine electrocardiography (ECG) and photoplethysmography (PPG), requiring multiple synchronized sensor types. PPG-only estimation offers a simpler acquisition setup but remains challenging because BP-related morphological information must be extracted in the presence of motion artifacts and high-frequency noise. This paper introduces TransfoRhythm, a Transformer-based DNN framework for PPG-only BP estimation using the MIMIC-IV Waveform Database. The framework uses multi-head attention to model temporal relationships among cycle-level PPG features. Evaluation was performed using patient-independent 5-fold cross-validation, with patient IDs used as the splitting unit and zero patient overlap between training and test folds. Within each fold, feature selection, collinearity filtering, data scaling, hyperparameter selection, and model fitting were performed using only the training patients. Under this protocol, TransfoRhythm achieved mean MAEs of mmHg for systolic BP and mmHg for diastolic BP, with corresponding RMSE values of and mmHg. The mean errors were mmHg and mmHg, while the mean values were and for systolic and diastolic BP, respectively. These findings demonstrate consistent predictive performance across held-out patient groups within the evaluated MIMIC-IV cohort. External and prospective validation remains necessary to establish generalizability beyond this dataset.

Unsupervised anomaly detection in software-defined networks via BiGAN-based traffic reconstruction and explainable artificial intelligence
abstract: The increasing reliance on computer networks across various environments underscores the critical need for effective intrusion detection mechanisms. In this manner, this paper presents an unsupervised anomaly detection system for Software-Defined Networks (SDN) based on traffic reconstruction using Bidirectional Generative Adversarial Networks (BiGAN). The proposed system operates in three phases: data collection and preprocessing, anomaly detection through traffic reconstruction and thresholding, and mitigation by blocking malicious IP addresses via dynamic updates to trust and blocklist entries. The system was evaluated using two public datasets, achieving high accuracy and robustness, particularly when utilizing the most significant traffic feature identified via SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) explainability technique. Results demonstrated our IDS’s capability to differentiate between normal and anomalous traffic. Additionally, the system’s effectiveness in mitigating attacks reached more than 93% of malicious flows, while ensuring minimal or no impact on legitimate traffic in both datasets. These findings highlight the system’s effectiveness in SDN environments, offering a consistent solution for proactive network anomaly detection and response.

DISCO: Component-wise update-period scheduling for medical image fine-tuning
abstract: Fine-tuning pretrained vision models is widely used for medical image classification. In conventional full fine-tuning and parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) pipelines, parameters selected for adaptation are commonly optimized under a uniform per-step update schedule. We observe that update period critically affects fine-tuning behavior, and that per-step updates are not universally optimal across datasets and architectures. Motivated by this observation, we propose DIS crete CO mponent updates ( DISCO ), a component-wise update-period scheduling framework for medical image fine-tuning. DISCO does not aim to serve as a general-purpose periodic optimizer; instead, it focuses on assigning heterogeneous update periods to functionally distinct lightweight adaptation components. Specifically, DISCO combines a slowly updated Coarse Adaptation Unit ( CAU ) for stable global adaptation with a faster Multi-period Support Unit ( MPU ) for fine-grained residual adaptation. These components are optimized through buffered periodic updates with component-specific update triggers, thereby separating the functional role of an adaptation module from its update period. Experiments on eight public medical imaging datasets across four modalities show that DISCO improves both full fine-tuning and PEFT baselines, suggesting that component-wise update-period scheduling is a useful and previously less emphasized design choice for medical image fine-tuning.

An adaptive lifelong incremental learning framework for power quality disturbance detection under concept drift
abstract: The expeditious rise in renewable penetration, inverter-based resources, electric vehicle charging infrastructure, and evolving load composition has driven significant concept drift and new power quality disturbance (PQD) patterns in modern power grids. As a result, contemporary static classifiers become progressively ineffective. To address this challenge, this paper proposes an adaptive lifelong incremental learning framework unified with drift detection, active online learning, and physics-based interpretability for PQD detection and classification under concept drift. Within a unified closed-loop classification architecture, four incremental learning strategies are systematically investigated: Fine-Tuning, Elastic Weight Consolidation (EWC)-Only, Replay-Only, Hybrid (with two additonal configurations of Hybrid-Abrupt and Hybrid-Mixed). The Hybrid strategy combines EWC, herding-based coreset replay, knowledge distillation, prototype regularization, and dark experience replay (DER), together with a dynamically expandable classification head. These methods are evaluated on a testbed of 20 PQDs divided into four tasks. The Hybrid method achieves the maximum accuracy ( ) with a forgetting rate of just and a Macro F1 of , validated across three seeds. A comparative analysis against continual learning baselines—iCaRL, GEM, DER , ER-ACE, and Cumulative-Oracle—demonstrates the competitive performance of the Hybrid approach. For drift detection, a KNN-embedded technique is evaluated against the established ADaptive WINdowing (ADWIN) and Drift Detection Method (DDM) techniques and is found to consistently achieve superior performance under evolving disturbance conditions. The proposed models use a ResNet-MLP-based encoder backbone; to validate its strength, the Hybrid method is additionally examined using Plain-MLP, Deep-MLP, MLP-No-BN, Transformer-Encoder, CNN-1D, and CNN-LSTM encoders. Physics-aligned features—root-mean-square (RMS) voltage and total harmonic distortion (THD)—serve dual roles as interpretable monitoring metrics and drift attribution indicators. A detailed computational complexity analysis is conducted, covering time, space, computational (FLOPs), and sample/scalability complexity. The six frameworks are further assessed under 27 noise scenarios spanning 9 categories—Pink and Brownian noise, additive white Gaussian noise (AWGN), impulsive noise, load harmonics, non-stationary mixed noise, communication signal drop, environmental flicker, and measurement bias. For the first time in the PQD literature, a comprehensive bifurcation analysis identifies the regime boundaries governed by EWC weight and noise intensity , complemented by a parametric sensitivity analysis of the proposed models. All six models are further exposed to (i) grid topology and (ii) renewable and power-electronics disturbance scenarios for realistic, system-level examination. Finally, validation on the XPQRS benchmark dataset (four tasks) shows the Hybrid-Mixed model achieving the best accuracy of 85.75 % with a forgetting rate of just 1.50 %. The complete framework was further validated through Processor-in-the-Loop (PIL) testing on a Raspberry Pi 5, confirming functional correctness of the full inference pipeline under embedded execution with an inference latency of approximately 0.15 ms/sample and a memory footprint of only 0.40 MB. Altogether, the developed models offer an effective, interpretable, and computationally-efficient approach for PQD detection under evolving grid conditions, providing a standard of comparison for future approaches in PQD analysis.

An extended agent-based Physarum polycephalum Model with repellent-driven behaviour
abstract: Physarum polycephalum is a remarkable single-celled amoeboid organism that exhibits unique computational capabilities during its plasmodium phase. Various algorithms have been developed to simulate its behaviour, including an agent-based model by Jones (2010) that effectively mimics the organism’s pattern-forming abilities and can approximate solutions to certain distance-based problems. However, the original algorithm lacks the mechanisms required to appropriately model responses to repellent stimuli, limiting its applicability to more complex environments. To address these limitations, we propose an enhanced version of the algorithm that incorporates a unified representation of attractants and repellents, along with a refined set of agent sensory and movement rules enabling active repulsion and dynamic speed adjustment. These enhancements significantly improve performance on problems the original algorithm could already solve, while also enabling it to solve problems it previously could not. This is demonstrated using the Euclidean Steiner tree problem and the Voronoi diagram problem. While the original algorithm can approximate solutions to the Euclidean Steiner tree problem, the extended version achieves equally accurate approximations with up to 65% fewer iterations. Moreover, the original algorithm fails to approximate Voronoi diagrams, whereas the extended algorithm successfully generates notably accurate approximations. Although the proposed modifications do not strictly adhere to the physical laws governing biological Physarum , these deliberate deviations significantly improve the algorithm’s effectiveness as a computational tool for solving Euclidean optimisation problems, potentially improving its applicability to problems such as spatial partitioning, network formation, and obstacle avoidance.

Knowledge-informed neural network for reliable and explainable prediction of concrete strength
abstract: Predicting compressive strength of concrete is crucial for optimized mix design for engineering properties and performance. While machine learning models are used for prediction, their effectiveness is often limited by challenges related to generalizability and scalability. This study developed knowledge-informed neural network (KINN) to predict compressive strength of concrete by integrating the empirical equation of concrete strength growth into hybrid loss function based on a large dataset from field projects. The performance of KINN is compared with other models including artificial neural networks (ANN), support vector regression (SVR), k-nearest neighbors (KNN), random forest (RF), eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) and the empirical equation. The results demonstrate that KINN achieves superior predictive stability and physical consistency compared to ANN having identical architecture, while offering competitive accuracy. Compared with tree-based ensemble methods (XGBoost, RF), KINN presents a trade-off: slightly lower mean R² but substantially reduced variability and physically consistent predictions aligned with domain knowledge. Furthermore, the SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis reveals that knowledge-informed models not only capture the underlying physical principles but are also more interpretable for the effect of water-binder ratio. Partial dependence plots and Accumulated Local Effects (ALE) are employed to investigate the effects of curing ages, water-to-binder ratio and percentage of supplemental cementitious materials (SCM) on compressive strength, providing valuable insights for engineering decision making. The integration of empirical knowledge into machine learning models, as demonstrated by KINN, enables engineers to incorporate prior domain expertise into predictions of concrete performance.

title: Online high-precision prediction method for injection molding product weight by integrating time-series/non-time-series mixed features and feature attention mechanism
abstract: To address the challenges of untimely detection and online monitoring lag in injection molding quality anomalies, this study proposes a mixed feature attention-artificial neural network (MFA-ANN) model for high-precision online prediction of product weight. By integrating mechanism-based with data-driven analysis, the proposed architecture decouples time series data (e.g., melt flow dynamics, thermal profiles) from non-time series data (e.g., mold features, pressure settings), enabling hierarchical feature extraction. A self-attention mechanism is strategically embedded during cross-domain feature fusion to dynamically calibrate inter-modality feature weights, thereby emphasizing critical determinants of weight variability. The results demonstrate that the MFA-ANN model achieves a RMSE of 0.0281 with 0.5 g weight fluctuation tolerance, outperforming conventional benchmarks: a 25.1% accuracy improvement over non-time series ANN models, 23.0% over LSTM networks, 25.7% over SVR, and 15.6% over RF models, respectively. Ablation studies quantitatively validate the synergistic enhancement derived from the integration of mixed feature modeling (contributing 22.4%) and the attention mechanism (contributing 11.2%), significantly enhancing the model's adaptability to varying working conditions and its resistance to noise. Moreover, critical sensitivity analyses further reveal that data resolution significantly impacts prediction reliability, low-fidelity sensor inputs degrade performance by 23.8% RMSE compared to high-precision measurements. Overall, this study provides an efficient and reliable solution for the intelligent quality control of injection molding processes.

title: T-S fuzzy-based robust stability control for semi-trailer trucks by integrating tractor yaw moment and trailer active steering
Temporal fusion transformer and deep state-space model for hydrogen-integrated power systems
abstract: Hydrogen is becoming a key element of modern power grids by enabling large-scale energy storage, renewable integration, sector coupling, and low-carbon operation. In hydrogen-integrated power networks, accurate hydrogen-demand modeling is essential for reliable scheduling, storage management, and system operation. To address this challenge, this study proposes a hybrid forecasting framework that combines energy-driven multistage decomposition, probabilistic residual modeling, and a hybrid learning head that selects either a Temporal Fusion Transformer (TFT) or a Deep State-Space Model (DSSM) for each component. The framework decomposes each series into intrinsic mode functions (IMFs) and a residual component, then iteratively refines the IMFs through feedback coupling and energy-guided updates to suppress noise while preserving dynamics. A Gaussian model enhanced by meta-learning over multiple kernels captures uncertainty, drift, and long-horizon structure. Hierarchical multi-resolution fusion integrates temporal and spectral cues, while the hybrid TFT-DSSM head generates calibrated quantile forecasts for each component and recombines them into final predictions. Empirical validation on two energy-related datasets confirmed the effectiveness of the proposed framework. On the hydrogen bus demand dataset, the model achieved an MAE of 2.1127, an MSE of 35.8056, an RMSE of 5.9838, and a MAPE of 14.0780%. On the Brent crude oil price dataset, the proposed model reduced test errors by 56.60% in MAE, 81.56% in MSE, 56.58% in MAPE, and 57.09% in RMSE relative to the baseline TFT-DSSM. Compared with EEMD-TFT-DSSM, it further improved forecasting accuracy, yielding reductions of 17.70% in MAE, 29.70% in MSE, 19.74% in MAPE, and 15.97% in RMSE.

title: Structural health monitoring of corrosion depth of buried pipelines by developing an interpretable stacking ensemble model CGEK-PipeCorr
A complexity-driven resampling approach for imbalanced learning
abstract: Imbalanced datasets pose significant challenges for machine learning (ML) models, which often lead to biased decisions and poor predictions for the minority class. While existing resampling methods address class imbalance, they sometimes neglect data complexity, which can lead to suboptimal performance in complex distributions. To address this, we propose a complexity-driven resampling method using two-stage clustering. For the majority class, K-Means and hierarchical clustering identify and remove extremely hard-to-classify samples based on complexity measures. For the minority class, K-Means clustering is applied first, and then new samples are generated within each cluster based on cluster complexity. The aim of this approach is to balance the datasets while preserving their inherent distribution. By employing different clustering methods at various stages, the method effectively captures clusters of diverse shapes and sizes, thereby enhancing clustering performance on complex datasets. The proposed method is then evaluated using three popular ML models on 27 public datasets from KEEL and four additional datasets from Kaggle using a rigorous 5-fold cross-validation protocol. The results show that the method significantly improves ML classifiers’ performance for imbalanced datasets, achieving the best average F1-Scores and Recall, alongside highly competitive G-Mean and AUC scores, compared to traditional baselines and recent state-of-the-art resampling techniques. This study indicates that dataset complexity significantly affects the performance of most ML models, indicating that careful consideration should be given when choosing resampling strategies for ML models when the dataset becomes more complex. Ultimately, the proposed method provides a highly reliable framework for real-world scenarios characterized by severe class overlap and noisy feature spaces, ensuring that underlying data structures are preserved during the resampling process.

title: A global-local deep decoupling and alignment framework for zero-shot industrial anomaly detection with vision-language models
Real-time physics-informed reconstruction of transient fields using sensor guidance and higher-order time differentiation
abstract: This study proposes FTI-PBSM (Fixed-Time-Increment Physics-informed neural network-Based Surrogate Model), a novel physics-informed surrogate modeling framework designed for real-time reconstruction of transient responses in time-dependent Partial Differential Equations (PDEs) using only sparse, time-dependent sensor measurements. Unlike conventional Physics-Informed Neural Network (PINN)-based models that rely on Automatic Differentiation (AD) over both spatial and temporal domains and require dedicated causal network architectures to impose temporal causality, the proposed approach entirely removes AD in the time direction. Instead, it leverages higher-order numerical differentiation methods, such as the Central Difference, Adams-Bashforth, and Backward Differentiation Formula, to explicitly impose temporal causality. This leads to a simplified model architecture with improved training stability, computational efficiency, and extrapolation capability. Furthermore, FTI-PBSM is trained on sparse sensor measurements from multiple PDE cases generated by varying PDE coefficients, with the sensor data serving as model input. This enables the model to learn a parametric PDE family and generalize to unseen physical cases, accurately reconstructing full-field transient solutions in real time. The proposed model is validated on four representative PDE problems-the convection equation, diffusion-reaction dynamics, Korteweg-de Vries (KdV) equation, and Allen-Cahn equation-and demonstrates superior prediction accuracy and generalization performance compared to a causal PBSM, which is used as the baseline model, in both interpolation and extrapolation tasks. It also shows strong robustness to sensor noise and variations in training data size, while significantly reducing training time.

The history-based adaptive multi-stage threshold accepting algorithm
abstract: Metaheuristics are a set of search methods which aim to provide high quality solutions to computationally hard optimisation problems, typically containing many components to control the search process. In single-point metaheuristic frameworks, a core component is the move acceptance method , which accepts or rejects a given modification to a solution, influencing the trajectory through the search space. In the case of cross-domain search, where a single search method aims to solve problem instances from multiple different domains, existing move acceptance methods tend to solve a few similar problems well. However, previous work has demonstrated that they under-perform when tasked with solving characteristically different problems, requiring expert intervention to reconfigure them for each domain individually. In this paper, a general purpose move acceptance method, History-based Adaptive Multi-Stage Threshold Accepting (HAMSTA), is proposed and tested for cross-domain search. HAMSTA is designed to exploit the strengths of a number of existing move acceptance strategies, with a set of internal mechanisms that adapt to the problem instance being solved, reducing the dependence on sensitive external parameters that require extensive tuning. The results show that using a single configuration across nine different problem domains, HAMSTA outperforms eight well-known existing move acceptance methods, including Simulated Annealing, even when those methods are re-tuned specifically for each domain.

Towards explainable and fair recommender systems: A survey of methods, taxonomies, and challenges
abstract: Abstract Recommender systems have become a fundamental component of modern online platforms,significantly influencing user experiences by delivering personalized content. However, theincreasing complexity of contemporary recommendation models has raised critical concernsregarding their transparency and fairness. This survey provides a comprehensive and unifiedreview of explainable and fair recommender systems, emphasizing the need to move beyondaccuracy-centric design toward trustworthy and responsible recommendation paradigms. Wefirst introduce the core concepts of recommender systems, explainability, and fairness, anddiscuss their roles in building transparent and accountable systems. We then propose a multidimensional taxonomy that systematically categorizes existing approaches based on objectives,intervention stages, explanation types, and fairness perspectives. Furthermore, we present adetailed analysis of state-of-the-art methods, including explainable recommendation techniques,fairness-aware models, and emerging approaches that jointly address both aspects. In addition,we examine commonly used evaluation metrics and provide a comprehensive analysis of thetrade-offs among accuracy, explainability, and fairness, highlighting the challenges of multiobjective optimization in real-world systems. Finally, we identify key open challenges, includingdata bias, methodological limitations, evaluation inconsistencies, and deployment constraints,and outline promising directions for future research. This survey aims to provide researchers andpractitioners with a unified perspective and to support the development of recommender systemsthat are not only accurate, but also transparent, fair, and trustworthy

A soft computing framework combining machine learning and constrained genetic optimization to maximize wheat yield under drought for climate change adaptation
abstract: Climate change, subsequent global warming, and population growth continuously increase the demand for food, making it necessary to improve agricultural production and, in particular, to breed high-yielding, drought-tolerant wheat capable of safeguarding long-term sustainability and food supply. Traditional breeding methods face limitations in achieving efficient genetic improvement. In this context, this study casts wheat yield estimation within a soft computing paradigm and examines how machine learning models (MLMs) can be tuned for wheat grain yield (GY) value prediction from yield components across a broad panel of wheat genotypes, with the aim of improving breeding efficiency under normal and drought stress conditions. Specifically, five MLMs are used to predict wheat GY based on yield component traits, with model selection performed through repeated genotype-grouped k-fold cross-validation that avoids information leakage among replicates of the same genotype. Then, a genetic optimization algorithm uses the best-performing neural network as its fitness function to identify an empirically-constrained candidate ideotype, i.e., a model-derived target combination of yield-component values that maximizes the predicted GY, subject to an applicability-domain penalty that keeps solutions within the observed trait space and a correlation-consistency penalty that preserves the empirical trait correlations. The choice of the best-performing genotype has revealed that the multi-trait genotype-ideotype distance index (MGIDI) enhances selection accuracy and identifies five genotypes. The paper demonstrates that combining MLMs with a constrained genetic algorithm can significantly enhance wheat breeding by optimizing yield-related traits and improving drought tolerance, illustrating how soft computing can address high-dimensional design problems under uncertainty.

title: Self-adaptive federated domain generalization for privacy-preserving fault diagnosis
abstract: Deploying data-driven fault diagnosis across distributed industrial machines raises four coupled challenges: domain shift, generalization to unseen working conditions, data privacy constraints, and autonomous adaptation. Existing federated domain generalization methods exhibit critical limitations: their augmentation is rudimentary, they weight all peer classifiers uniformly, they lose substantial accuracy relative to centralized training, and none adapts autonomously at runtime. To address these challenges, we propose Self-Adaptive Federated Domain Generalization (SAFDG), a framework that integrates Monitor-Analyze-Plan-Execute-Knowledge (MAPE-K) autonomic control with federated domain generalization, autonomously selecting between local and federated adaptation based on data availability while achieving robust performance under unseen conditions with minimal centralized-DG gap. The proposed approach integrates four mechanisms: domain-aware interpolation targets distributional gaps with contrastive alignment, cross-classification consistency trains feature extractors against frozen peer classifiers, adversarial discrimination suppresses domain biases, and confidence-based fusion dynamically weights classifiers. On four bearing datasets across 24 test case conditions, SAFDG achieves accuracy (cross-machine) and (cross-bearing), outperforming the strongest privacy-preserving competitors by 2.7–5.7 points, with centralized-DG gaps of only 3.0 and 1.8 points, respectively. A runtime replay shows the loop switching pathways autonomously as working conditions evolve, and ablation studies show that the four mechanisms reinforce one another, with their combined effect exceeding the sum of individual contributions.

Hiding identities, keeping emotions: A systematic review of de-identification methods for computational-intelligence–based emotion recognition
abstract: Emotion recognition systems frequently depend on sensitive personal data, such as facial expressions, voice patterns, and textual input, making privacy protection a critical concern. This review provides a comprehensive analysis of emotion-preserving anonymization methods, focusing on their application to emotion classification tasks. Using the PRISMA methodology, a systematic literature review was conducted across multiple databases, including Google Scholar, PubMED, Medline, Embase, PMC, NCBI Bookshelf, and NIH Manuscripts. Searches spanned a decade (2014–2024) and employed queries such as “anonymization + emotion,” “privacy + preserve + emotion,” and “de-identification + emotion,” yielding 49,700 initial results. After removing duplicates and manual screening, 70 publications were selected for in-depth analysis. The study categorizes de-identification techniques, emphasizing their effectiveness in maintaining emotional cues while safeguarding individual identities across multi-modal datasets. A systematic evaluation of these methods reveals trade-offs between privacy protection and data utility, with particular attention to the accuracy of emotion classification after anonymization. The review identifies gaps in current approaches, including the need for advanced techniques optimized for multi-modal datasets, cross-cultural robustness, and real-world applicability in privacy-sensitive domains such as mental health or education. This review emphasizes the importance of advancing privacy-preserving anonymization techniques, which enables ethical emotion recognition research, while preserving the privacy of individuals.
